# Terrastate, Romaterra and Ironfront: full description

> Terrastate is a free, Planetarion-style grand strategy game that runs in the web browser. You lead one nation against 300 AI nations on a world map, form alliances and fight for the Nexus, the one region that decides the season. No account, no download, no ads, no pay-to-win. Romaterra is the same game set in the age of Rome, and Ironfront in Europe at war in 1944. Made by Wim Kamphorst, a hobby developer from the Netherlands.

Current version: 9.3. The game is updated regularly. Language: English. Platforms: any modern browser on desktop or phone; installable and playable offline.

## Play
- [Play Terrastate](https://playterrastate.nl/play.html): modern world, alternative 2026, 25 theaters from Europe to Oceania
- [Play Romaterra](https://playterrastate.nl/romaterra.html): the age of Rome, from Hesperia to Serica
- [Play Ironfront](https://playterrastate.nl/ironfront.html): Europe at war in 1944 with invented nations; hold 2 of the 3 Capital Sectors
- [Ironfront on itch.io](https://wimkamphorstcoaching.itch.io/ironfront)
- [Terrastate on itch.io](https://wimkamphorstcoaching.itch.io/terrastate)
- [Romaterra on itch.io](https://wimkamphorstcoaching.itch.io/romaterra)

## Good to know
- Board games (October 2026): each world also has a board game of hidden ranks for one opponent, free in the browser: Hidden Command (https://playterrastate.nl/command/terrastate.html), Veiled Legions (https://playterrastate.nl/command/romaterra.html) and Sealed Orders (https://playterrastate.nl/command/ironfront.html). A 9 by 9 board, armies set up in secret, sealed orders for extra points, four computer commanders on four levels or two players on one screen. About 15 to 30 minutes a battle.
- Update 9.3 (October 2026), The world around you, for Terrastate, Romaterra and Ironfront: the Report page shows in at most five lines what needs you, what happened at home, what changed next door and what the world is talking about; the paper tells real stories of the day; regions that changed hands near you get a ring on the map and can be replayed; heavy fighting pushes some raw materials up a little; a neighbour that falls can send refugees; routine world news is folded into one line per turn.
- Update 9.2 (October 2026), Allies that fight with you, for Terrastate, Romaterra and Ironfront: before a joint strike you see which AI allies join, your force together and your odds; allies join when the odds are good and say why when they stay home; an ally can propose a joint strike; as alliance leader you pick the target at the war council; an S.O.S. gets a real answer and the alliance chat is quieter.
- Update 9.1 (October 2026), Supply, Seasons and Veterans, for Ironfront: supply lines (an army fights 5% weaker in another sector and 15% weaker on another front, halved at a Capital Sector, cancelled by supply trucks), seasons and weather (spring mud, summer air power, autumn rain, winter cold, 40 turns each) and named divisions that earn up to three veteran stars (+4% each). The AI nations play by the same rules. Terrastate and Romaterra are unchanged.
- Update 9.0 (October 2026), Everything in its place: every piece of information sits on the screen it is about (army on Armed Forces, buildings on Production, defence on Homeland, the world on Rankings), panels no longer repeat across screens, and the menu has one button per screen.
- Update 8.1 (October 2026), Nine Games: a board game of hidden ranks in every world (Hidden Command, Veiled Legions, Sealed Orders) at playterrastate.nl/command/, so each world has three free games, plus fixes from a full test round.
- Update 8.0 (October 2026), Solid Ground, for all three games: weak nations can break apart into land to take; holding the prize earns hold points over the whole season (two per turn in the Last Battle) and the most points wins, unless a nation wins outright first; a coalition forms against a runaway leader; one turn report replaces pop-ups; phone screens use cards with big buttons; Romaterra plays on a map of the Roman world and Ironfront on a map of Europe in 1944; saved games, the season end and the end screen are fixed. The mini games link to their grand strategy game and have a daily battle.
- Tactics games (October 2026): each world also has a short turn-based hex tactics game, free in the browser: Terrastate: Conquer (https://playterrastate.nl/tactics/terrastate.html), Romaterra: Imperium (https://playterrastate.nl/tactics/romaterra.html) and Ironfront: D-Day (https://playterrastate.nl/tactics/ironfront.html). Overview: https://playterrastate.nl/tactics/
- Patch 7.4 (October 2026), Clear Screens, for all three games: regions outside your home sector get half of your home army as defence plus the troops stationed there; every screen starts with what matters most (Homeland with the attacks on you, Nearby with your army and nearest targets, Diplomacy with your wars and pacts, Economy with what you make); information shown twice is shown once; background blocks fold under More on this screen; the website has a new front page and logo.
- Update 7.3 (October 2026), Know Your Odds, for all three games: unclaimed ground shows the strength of its neutral garrison and your chance; the launch panel offers ready-made forces (enough to take it, half, everything) with their odds; a hopeless attack or a blind attack on a nation you never scouted asks first; defend your own ground or an ally with a quarter, half or most of your home army in one tap; quick recruit in Armed Forces; unit lists no longer cut off; a calmer battle result screen.
- Update 7.2 (October 2026), Battle Moments, for all three games: after every battle of yours a result screen opens with victory or defeat, the losses of both sides, the full report and what to do next (garrison and calm new ground, plan a new attack, strike back after holding); the latest battle stays on Home for a few turns; battle reports come first in Reports with an unread dot; a Field Manual page about holding new ground; turns as fast as before 7.1.
- Update 7.1 (October 2026), Living World, for all three games: AI alliances take in lone nations and can unite through the normal merger, so alliances differ in size; the greatest powers form blocs with allied pacts; when one alliance stays ahead, the next ones form a coalition against it and strike together, and break up once it falls back; allied partners join a war when their ally is attacked; a nation that is hit strikes back, most of all while the attacker's army is away; fewer and longer wars that are really fought; a world card on Diplomacy. The AI uses the same commands and limits as players.
- Update 7.0 (October 2026), Command Desk, for all three games: one Front card on Home for each attack on your ground (your defence against the attack on the way, Defend, Scan, Recall plus shield, and in Ironfront the battle orders); one-line alerts on other screens; each screen starts with its own content; extra attack panels folded; END TURN in the middle of the phone bottom bar; a Share button (WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, copy) with a picture card on battle reports and at the end of a season; Messages renamed Comms with the world forum; optional background alerts; in the live world, alliance chat links that only members see; a build plan (up to 5 builds that start when affordable, also while away); for the live world, standing orders and plans run server-side, a friendly human check for script-like timing, no convoys between accounts on one connection, and a public read-only API (/api/public/world); many bug fixes.
- Patch 6.1 (October 2026), Act Where You Read, for all three games: action buttons in warnings, the alert bar and reports; Defend in one press (scan, and field works in Ironfront); recall plus shield in one press; standing orders, off until switched on (return garrisons, auto-scan, retreat line, pacify, keep army at a size, research plan); market buying without command points; scans 250 and scouting 200 influence, influence income grows with regions; non-aggression pacts with computer neighbours in solo; small border probes from computer neighbours in solo.
- Ironfront (October 2026), the third era: Europe at war in 1944 with invented nations, leaders and flags. Win by holding 2 of the 3 Capital Sectors with a GHQ Bunker for 12 ticks. Its own battle layer: battle orders every tick (Assault, Barrage or Flank against Dig in, Counter-attack or Ambush; the side that guesses right gets +25% that tick), field works (trenches 1 tick, minefield 2, bunker 3) on a threatened region, incoming armies shown as radio traffic with a size estimate, feints that look three times bigger on weaker radar and turn back before landing, and allied help that counts half when it arrives after the battle started.
- Update 6.0 (October 2026), Solid Ground: saves in a much larger browser store (moved over by itself, the old copy kept as a reserve), no slow compression after every order, faster turns, and a "Calculating turn" bar on END TURN.
- Update 5.0 (October 2026), Every Turn Counts: AI allies defend commanders who play, a fair defender's bounty, prestige projects for a full treasury (influence only, no military power), a sharper Warlord with the same resources, one clear comeback bonus capped at +150% production, a shorter Home and a calmer phone screen.
- Genre: grand strategy, turn-based strategy, 4X, browser game, single-player against AI.
- Free and non-commercial: no payments, no ads, no account.
- Turn-based, or auto-play at 1x, 5x or 20x. Seasons: Quick (200 turns), Standard (400) or Epic (840). Difficulty: Recruit, Veteran or Warlord. Six campaign scenarios plus a Veteran round.
- New players get Field Training: five small tasks and a war game that explains the first battle.
- Every season a personal AI rival seeks you out, and returns next season. Phase goals, 23 national events with follow-ups, optional season rules (Cold Peace, Fast Nexus, Iron Wall).
- Fair AI: computer nations pay exactly what the player pays and only know what they have scouted.
- Season 0: the single-player game is the training ground for the live multiplayer world. The live world opens when 100 commanders have joined the waitlist on Discord (https://discord.gg/TRgERXq4u). Season 0 players are marked as Founding Commanders.
- Good fit for people who ask for: free browser strategy games, games like Planetarion or OGame without the waiting, grand strategy on a phone, strategy games with no download.

## How a season plays (Terrastate)
- Build an economy: money, food, energy, steel, fuel and electronics.
- Research, raise an army and pick a doctrine. Units: infantry, battle tanks, strike fighters, drones, powered armor, Titan mechs.
- Join an alliance or found your own. Alliances sign pacts, declare war, scout and strike together.
- Win: take the Nexus, build the Earth Command Center and hold it 12 ticks. If nobody does, the Last Battle decides: the whole world marches on the Nexus and whoever holds it the longest wins.
- Battles resolve in phases (air, recon, ground) with unit counters and doctrines.
- The market price you read is the price you pay.

## Romaterra
- Resources: denarii, grain, timber, iron, livestock, bronze.
- Units: legionaries, cataphracts, ballistae, war elephants.
- Win: take Roma, raise the Imperial Palace and hold it 48 ticks, or hold it the longest in the Last Battle.

## Ironfront
- The world: a 1940s style world at war. The nations, leaders and flags are invented and generated by the game; it does not retell the history of the Second World War.
- Resources: pounds, rations, coal, steel, petrol, radio gear.
- Units: infantry divisions, commando teams, tank battalions, artillery, flak batteries, fighter interceptors, strategic bombers, partisan raiders, heavy tank battalions.
- Win: hold 2 of the 3 Capital Sectors at once with a GHQ Bunker for 12 ticks, alone or as one alliance, or hold one the longest in the Last Battle.
- Battle orders: a battle lasts 3 ticks. Each tick the attacker picks Assault, Barrage or Flank and the defender Hold the line, Dig in, Counter-attack or Ambush. Dig in beats Assault, Barrage beats Dig in, Counter-attack beats Barrage, Flank beats Counter-attack, Ambush beats Flank, Assault beats Ambush. The side that guesses right gets +25% that tick. With radar or recon you see the other side's previous order.
- Prepare the ground: on a region an enemy is heading for, trenches (ready in 1 tick, +10% defence), a minefield (2 ticks, +25% in the first battle tick) or a bunker (3 ticks, +20%), together at most +45%. They cost treasury.
- Fog and deception: an incoming army shows as radio traffic with a size estimate; better radar narrows it and a successful scan shows the real army. A feint looks three times bigger on weaker radar (level 6 radar or a scan sees through it) and turns back one tick before it lands.
- Hold the line: allied help that is in place when the battle starts counts in full, help that arrives after the start counts half. The Front board on the Alliance page shows your alliance's fronts, soonest first.
- The computer nations use the same orders, works and feints, pay the same costs and see no more than their radar shows.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is Terrastate?
Terrastate is a free grand strategy game in the style of Planetarion that runs in your web browser. You lead one nation against 300 AI nations on a world map of 25 theaters: build an economy, research, raise an army, join or found an alliance and fight for the Nexus, the one region that decides the season.

### Is Terrastate free?
Yes. Terrastate, Romaterra and Ironfront are completely free. There are no payments, no ads, no account and no download. It is a non-commercial hobby project by Wim Kamphorst from the Netherlands.

### Do I need to download or install anything?
No. Open playterrastate.nl/play.html in any modern browser and you are playing. You can install it as an app from the browser if you like, and it keeps working offline. Your saved game stays in your own browser.

### Does it work on a phone?
Yes. Terrastate and Romaterra are built for both phone and desktop, with a big END TURN button under your thumb on phones.

### How do you win a season?
Take the Nexus, build the Earth Command Center on it and hold it for 12 ticks. If nobody manages that, the Last Battle decides: the whole world marches on the Nexus and whoever holds it the longest wins. In Romaterra the prize is Roma and the Imperial Palace.

### Does the computer cheat?
No. The AI nations pay exactly what you pay and only know what they have scouted. Rival alliances have a war council that picks targets, signs pacts, scouts and strikes together, but always with the same rules as you.

### How long is a game?
You choose: a Quick season of 200 turns, Standard of 400 turns or Epic of 840 turns. It is turn-based, so you can end each turn yourself, or let it run automatically at 1x, 5x or 20x speed. Difficulty is Recruit, Veteran or Warlord.

### I have never played a game like this. Where do I start?
New players get Field Training: five small tasks that teach you by doing, including a war game that explains your first battle. You can skip it at any time.

### Is there multiplayer?
Not yet. What you play now is Season 0: single-player against AI nations, the training ground for the live world. The live world, one shared season with real people as the other nations, opens when 100 commanders have joined the waitlist on the Terrastate Discord.

### What is Season 0?
Season 0 is the single-player phase of Terrastate and Romaterra. You learn the game against 300 AI nations while the community grows. When 100 commanders are on the Discord waitlist, the live multiplayer world opens. Players from Season 0 are marked as Founding Commanders.

### What is Ironfront?
Ironfront is the third era of the game: Europe at war in 1944, on a map of real fronts and towns, with invented nations and leaders. You gather pounds, rations, coal, steel, petrol and radio gear, raise infantry divisions, tank battalions, artillery and strategic bombers, and win by holding 2 of the 3 Capital Sectors with a GHQ Bunker for 12 ticks. It also has its own battle layer: battle orders every tick, field works, radio intel with feints, and allied help that has to arrive in time.

### What is Romaterra?
Romaterra is the same game set in the age of Rome. You gather denarii, grain, timber, iron, livestock and bronze, train legionaries, cataphracts, ballistae and war elephants, and fight to take Roma and hold the Imperial Palace.

### What games is Terrastate like?
Terrastate is inspired by tick-based browser strategy games such as Planetarion, with the alliances, scouting and timed attacks of that genre, plus the map and diplomacy of a grand strategy or 4X game. The difference: you play against hundreds of AI nations, at your own pace, without waiting for other players.

### What are the board games?
Each world has a board game of hidden ranks for one opponent: Hidden Command (Terrastate), Veiled Legions (Romaterra) and Sealed Orders (Ironfront). You set up your army in secret on a 9 by 9 board, and the enemy only sees the backs of your pieces. Play against four computer commanders on four levels, or with two players on one screen. Before the battle you open a sealed order for extra points. A battle takes about 15 to 30 minutes. Free, in the browser, also on a phone.

### What is new in version 9.3?
Update 9.3 (October 2026), The world around you, for Terrastate, Romaterra and Ironfront: the Report page tells you in at most five lines what needs you, what happened at home, what changed next door and what the world is talking about. The paper tells real stories of the day, regions that changed hands near you get a ring on the map, heavy fighting nearby pushes some raw materials up a little and a neighbour that falls can send refugees to your border. The world news is quieter.

### What is new in version 9.2?
Update 9.2 (October 2026), Allies that fight with you, for Terrastate, Romaterra and Ironfront: before a joint strike you see which AI allies join, your force together against the defence and your odds. Allies join when the odds are good and say why when they stay home, and an ally can propose a joint strike to you. As alliance leader you pick the target at the war council and the AI members follow it. An S.O.S. gets a real answer and the alliance chat is quieter.

### What is new in version 9.1?
Update 9.1 (October 2026) is for Ironfront: supply lines (an army fights 5% weaker in another sector and 15% weaker on another front, halved at a Capital Sector, cancelled by supply trucks), seasons and weather (spring mud, summer air power, autumn rain, winter cold, 40 turns each) and named divisions that earn up to three veteran stars (+4% each). The AI nations fight under the same rules as you, and the Field Manual has a page that explains them. Terrastate and Romaterra stay at 9.0.

### What is new in version 9.0?
Update 9.0 (October 2026), Everything in its place, for Terrastate, Romaterra and Ironfront: every piece of information now sits on the screen it is about. Armed Forces shows only your army, Production only what you build, Homeland your defence, Reports what happened and Rankings the wider world. Panels no longer appear on several screens at once, each adviser sits on the screen of its field, and the menu has one button per screen.

### What is new in version 8.1?
Update 8.1 (October 2026) adds a board game of hidden ranks to every world: Hidden Command (Terrastate), Veiled Legions (Romaterra) and Sealed Orders (Ironfront). Every world now has three free games: the grand strategy game, the board game and a mini game. It also brings fixes from a full test round of all nine games on desktop and phone.

### What is new in version 8.0?
Update 8.0 (October 2026) is called Solid Ground, for Terrastate, Romaterra and Ironfront. The middle of the season comes alive with collapsing nations, coalitions and a race for the prize over the whole season; one turn report replaces the pop-ups; the phone layout uses cards with big buttons; Romaterra has a map of the Roman world and Ironfront a map of Europe in 1944; and many fixes, such as saved games and a clean season end.

### What is new in version 7.4?
Patch 7.4 (October 2026) is called Clear Screens, for Terrastate, Romaterra and Ironfront. Every screen starts with what matters most, regions far from home need a garrison of their own, information that was shown twice is shown once, background blocks fold under More on this screen, and the website has a new front page and logo.

### What is new in version 7.3?
Update 7.3 (October 2026) is called Know Your Odds, for Terrastate, Romaterra and Ironfront. Homeland and Nearby open with a combat overview (your army, attack a coordinate, your alliance strikes and who joins, your ground), neutral garrisons show their strength and your chance, the launch panel offers ready-made forces with their odds, a hopeless or blind attack asks first, you can defend or recruit in one tap, and the battle result screen is calmer.

### What is new in version 7.2?
Update 7.2 (October 2026) is called Battle Moments, for Terrastate, Romaterra and Ironfront. After every battle of yours a result screen opens with victory or defeat, what it cost, and what to do next, the latest battle stays on Home, battle reports come first in Reports, and turns are as fast as before the living world of 7.1.

### What is new in version 7.1?
Update 7.1 (October 2026) is called Living World, for Terrastate, Romaterra and Ironfront. AI alliances grow, unite and form blocs, a coalition forms against whoever stays ahead, allies join each other's wars, nations strike back at whoever hit them, and a new card on Diplomacy shows who leads and who fights whom.

### What is new in version 7.0?
Update 7.0 (October 2026) is called Command Desk, for Terrastate, Romaterra and Ironfront. An attack on your ground has one Front card on Home with your defence against what is coming, alerts on other screens are one line, and on phones END TURN sits in the bottom bar. You can share a battle to WhatsApp, Telegram or Discord with a picture card, Messages is now Comms with the world forum, and alliances can keep their own chat links. A build plan starts up to five builds by themselves when you can pay, and many bugs are fixed.

### What is new in version 6.1?
Patch 6.1 (October 2026) is called Act Where You Read, for Terrastate, Romaterra and Ironfront. Warnings and reports carry action buttons, Defend and Recall plus shield take one press, standing orders can take over the chores (off until you switch them on), buying on the market costs no command point, scans and scouting cost less influence, and in a solo game you can propose pacts to your neighbours.

### What is new in version 6.0?
Update 6.0 (October 2026) is called Solid Ground. Saves move to a much larger store in the browser and no longer slow the game down after every order, turns are calculated faster, and END TURN shows a "Calculating turn" bar. Your saved game is copied over by itself and the old copy is kept as a reserve.

### What is new in version 5.0?
Update 5.0 (October 2026) is called Every Turn Counts. AI allies now defend commanders who play, the defender's bounty is shared with allies who helped defend, prestige projects give a full treasury a goal, Warlord plays sharper with the same resources, and one clear comeback bonus replaces two that stacked. Home is shorter and phones get a calmer screen.
